sourceSpec.title: Frontend-independent Rust Bridge for Windows and macOS
sourceSpec.description: Fresh Rust application engine and replaceable web frontend in a thin Tauri shell. UI iteration is a primary product goal: all first-release flows must run against deterministic typed mocks without game/native/backend dependencies. Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS are independently planned and qualified. Intel Mac host support is outside this release; actual game process architecture on Apple Silicon still governs injected payload pairing. Existing behavior and test scenarios inform requirements; C#/WPF implementation preservation is not a constraint. Canonical Profiles and producer ownership remain separate.
acceptanceCriteria: Rust engine and domain have no Tauri/webview dependencies; CLI and UI use one command/event contract.
Mock browser development supports all player journeys and failure/progress/draft/recovery states without native dependencies.
One visible install/profile selection with captured operation targets; ordinary and isolated requests remain distinct.
Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS have actual build, runtime, package and accessibility evidence.
Shared Profiles retains native catalog/storage/game update/exclusion ownership; no second catalog/updater.
Mod management, schema-driven settings/Data Sync, launch, game management, diagnostics and independent Bridge update are usable.
Plans/revisions/physical identities revalidated under retained exclusions; losing writers have no durable side effects.
Cancellation/disconnect/restart and fault recovery are honest and idempotent.
Three trust domains and per-platform artifact pairing/signing are independently verified.
Frontend semantic/accessibility/visual tests and actual WebView2/WKWebView UX qualification are required.
Dependency work is executed by explicit repo-scoped packets with real commands and receipts.
No placeholder gates, inferred account identity, reused WPF qualification or one-OS release substitution.
